children: Several of the world's advanced economies are expected to see borrowing costs rise over the next five years, even as they deal with already elevated debt, a post on the IMF blog said. "Rising Sovereign Yields Raise Financial Stakes" points out that the Group of Seven's average 10-year government bond yield rose by over 1 percentage point between February and September, to touch its highest level in over two decades. The post also said the effective average interest cost of government financing is seen rising from 2.3% in 2021 to 3.7% in 2031. The U.S., for example, is expected to see interest payments rise to 5.7% in 2031, after paying 2.8% prior to the pandemic, the post said. (stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)
